title: A printed layer must satisfy several constraints at once
caption: Small dimensions alone are insufficient: placement, shape and defect control must also hold across the wafer. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Feature dimensions
nodes.detail: The pattern must print to the intended size and shape.

nodes.label: Overlay
nodes.detail: New geometry must align with earlier layers.

nodes.label: Defect control
nodes.detail: Missing, bridged or malformed features threaten yield.

nodes.label: Usable layer
nodes.detail: The process must meet all requirements together.

source.heading: What a Litho Layer Has to Achieve

title: The track and scanner form one connected cell
caption: A controlled interface moves the wafer from film preparation to exposure and development. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Coat and bake
nodes.detail: The track establishes the resist film.

nodes.label: Expose in scanner
nodes.detail: The reticle image modifies the resist.

nodes.label: Post-exposure process
nodes.detail: Controlled baking develops the chemical change.

nodes.label: Develop
nodes.detail: The track converts solubility differences into a pattern.

source.heading: The Litho Cell at a Glance

title: Resist tone decides which regions remain
caption: Exposure changes solubility; the developer removes the soluble material rather than cutting the pattern mechanically. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Positive tone
nodes.detail: Exposed regions become more soluble and are removed.

nodes.label: Negative tone
nodes.detail: Exposed regions become less soluble and remain.

nodes.label: Development
nodes.detail: The liquid reveals the chemical contrast as geometry.

title: Each track step controls a different part of the film
caption: Surface preparation, solvent removal, reaction control and development cooperate to make a reproducible resist pattern. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Prepare the surface
nodes.detail: Prime for reliable resist adhesion.

nodes.label: Coat and soft bake
nodes.detail: Set thickness and remove excess solvent.

nodes.label: Post-exposure bake
nodes.detail: Control reaction extent and molecular movement.

nodes.label: Develop and inspect
nodes.detail: Reveal and check the resulting pattern.

source.heading: The Track Recipes, Step by Step

title: Resolution and focus tolerance compete
caption: Shorter wavelength and larger aperture improve imaging capability, while a larger aperture reduces depth of focus. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Wavelength
nodes.detail: The light's wavelength sets a fundamental imaging scale.

nodes.label: Numerical aperture
nodes.detail: A wider accepted cone carries more pattern information.

nodes.label: Focus tolerance
nodes.detail: The wafer surface must stay within the usable image plane range.

source.heading: The Optics: Resolution, Depth of Focus, and the Wavelength March

title: An immersion scanner synchronizes optics and motion
caption: The reticle and wafer move under coordinated control while the immersion liquid changes the final optical interface. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Reticle stage
nodes.detail: The master pattern is scanned through illumination.

nodes.label: Projection optics
nodes.detail: The optical system forms a reduced image.

nodes.label: Immersion interface
nodes.detail: Liquid lies between the final lens and wafer.

nodes.label: Wafer stage
nodes.detail: Position and height control align the moving surface.

source.heading: Anatomy of a 193 nm Immersion Scanner

title: A process window is a region, not one perfect setting
caption: Dose and focus interact; acceptable dimensions must survive realistic variation around the nominal recipe. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Dose variation
nodes.detail: Changing exposure energy shifts the printed response.

nodes.label: Focus variation
nodes.detail: Surface height and optical focus alter the image.

nodes.label: Acceptable overlap
nodes.detail: Only combinations meeting the feature limits are usable.

source.heading: Process Windows: Bossung Plots and the Focus-Exposure Matrix

title: Pre-distort the mask to improve the printed result
caption: Optical proximity correction compensates for imaging effects; the best mask geometry may look unlike the intended wafer geometry. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Target layout
nodes.detail: The designer specifies the desired wafer features.

nodes.label: Corrected mask
nodes.detail: OPC modifies shapes to compensate for the process.

nodes.label: Optical image
nodes.detail: Finite imaging capability transforms the mask pattern.

nodes.label: Printed result
nodes.detail: The goal is fidelity on the wafer, not on the mask.

title: Dense patterns can be built through different sequences
caption: Splitting exposures and creating sidewall spacers solve density limits through different mechanisms and error sources. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: LELE splitting
nodes.detail: Separate sparse masks combine into a denser result.

nodes.label: SADP spacers
nodes.detail: Sidewalls around a mandrel define new narrow features.

nodes.label: SAQP repetition
nodes.detail: Another spacer sequence further multiplies pattern density.

nodes.label: Cut or block masks
nodes.detail: Additional patterning removes unwanted connections.

title: A node uses more than one lithography method
caption: Layer geometry and cost determine the exposure route; a process node does not replace every layer with its most advanced scanner. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Critical fine layers
nodes.detail: The tightest geometries use the strongest available patterning methods.

nodes.label: Less demanding layers
nodes.detail: DUV remains useful where its capability is sufficient.

nodes.label: Multiple-patterned layers
nodes.detail: Some layouts require extra patterning steps.

source.heading: The Lithography Roadmap by Layer (as of 2026)

title: The scanner depends on specialized supply chains
caption: The lithography tool integrates optical, source, motion and control capabilities; market concentration reflects a system-level dependency. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Optical and source systems
nodes.detail: Specialists supply demanding illumination and imaging components.

nodes.label: Precision motion
nodes.detail: Stages and metrology synchronize position at speed.

nodes.label: Control and integration
nodes.detail: Software and system engineering coordinate the components.

nodes.label: Qualified scanner
nodes.detail: Integrated capability must work reliably in a fab.
